findings.title: Optimized paginator cannot paginate datetime-ordered audit logs
findings.body: `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint` selects `OptimizedCursorPaginator` while ordering `AuditLogEntry` by `-datetime`. This paginator's `get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly on the field value, which is a `datetime`, so building cursors for any non-empty optimized response raises `TypeError`. Even if that were avoided, `value_from_cursor` returns a numeric cursor value rather than converting it to a datetime for the subsequent queryset filter. Thus an administrator requesting `optimized_pagination=true` receives a 500 on a non-empty audit-log response. This endpoint needs a datetime-aware paginator (or the optimized paginator needs the DateTimePaginator key/cursor conversion behavior).

findings.title: Changing Redis collection type breaks existing buffered segments during rollout
findings.body: This writes each existing `span-buf:s:*` key with `ZADD`, whereas previously the same keys were Redis sets populated with `SADD`. Buffered keys can remain for up to `redis_ttl` (default one hour), so a rolling deployment will encounter old set keys: `ZADD` will return WRONGTYPE, and the new Lua script's `ZCARD`/`ZUNIONSTORE` and new flusher's `ZSCAN` likewise cannot operate on them. This can repeatedly fail consumer batches and prevent both ingestion and flushing until the old keys expire. Use versioned keys or provide a compatibility/migration path before switching the Redis data structure.

findings.title: Eviction ignores the configured max_segment_spans limit
findings.body: The buffer still exposes `max_segment_spans` as a constructor option, but the only span-count enforcement is now hard-coded to 1000 in Lua. The previous flush-side limit used `self.max_segment_spans`; after this change custom deployments cannot lower or raise the limit, and segments between their configured limit and 1000 are emitted rather than rejected/limited as configured. Pass the configured limit to the script and enforce that value, or remove/document the option and update callers if a fixed 1000-span contract is intentional.

findings.title: Redirect traversal limit is reduced and can split deep traces
findings.body: The redirect-chain traversal limit is reduced from 10,000 to 1,000. For a trace whose buffered parent chain exceeds 1,000 links, the script stops resolving redirects and attaches the arriving span to an intermediate buffer rather than the root buffer. Those buffers can then be queued and flushed as separate segments, producing incorrect segment IDs and incomplete trace segments. Retain the prior limit or add a safe chain-compression strategy rather than silently reducing the supported tree depth.
